If you have a normal dog, don't come here.
For years Theo was seen by Hanna, a proper vet who rolled up her sleeves, actually handled your dog and understood the context: animals get nervous at the vet. That's not news. Since she went back to Australia, this place has clearly lost its best vet.

Today I brought Theo in to get samples from some lumps on his back. We got Harry, who was cold from start to finish and seemed more interested in handing me the price list than in doing his job. I held Theo myself so he could take the first sample, and he got it. Theo then started barking and got defensive, which is exactly what a nervous dog does. Harry decided to take him downstairs to clean him up, away from me, and apparently he got even more stressed down there. Harry came back seemingly shocked that a dog would react like that to a syringe, and refused to do the second lump.

His solution? Sedate Theo and come back, and pay another consultation fee. So with the owner doing the holding, the job got done. Without me, a whole team couldn't handle one nervous dog, and I'm expected to pay twice for it. Hard not to conclude that the priority here is money, not the patient.

Throughout, he was very careful with his wording and kept apologising "on behalf of" everyone, but showed zero real interest in Theo. Polished language doesn't replace care. He even looked shocked when I told him I was leaving and wouldn't be coming back.

This feels like a practice not used to deal with real dogs with real reactions.

Hanna, you're missed. As for this practice, you've lost a patient and a client. We won't be back.
